findings.title: Ambiguous timestamp fallback can attach evidence to the wrong timeline entry
findings.what: matchesRef treats timestamp alone as identity whenever toolUseId is absent. If the saved entryIndex becomes stale and two entries in the same session have the same timestamp, findIndex selects the first match rather than the referenced entry or an unresolved result. Recommendation provenance can therefore silently display unrelated evidence while appearing successfully resolved.
findings.fix: When fallback candidates lack a stable toolUseId, collect all timestamp matches and resolve only if exactly one exists; otherwise return null. Prefer adding a stable per-entry identifier to EvidenceRef for all entry kinds when available.
findings.acceptance: Add a unit test with a stale index and two same-session entries sharing the referenced timestamp but different summaries and no toolUseId; resolveEvidenceRef must return null rather than either entry. Preserve successful unique-timestamp and toolUseId fallback cases.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read src/lib/evidence.ts:21-27 and 44-71 at the immutable baseline. The indexed path protects only an unchanged index; the fallback at lines 61-63 uses findIndex over matchesRef, and matchesRef checks only timestamp when toolUseId is absent. The dispatched tests cover unique timestamps and tool-id fallback but no duplicate-timestamp collision, so the misbinding remains reproducible.
